source.reported_by: Lopes de Moraes and De Losso (2026)

structural_lemma.premise: Finite deterministic frozen-state map F:S->S has exactly one terminal directed cycle.
structural_lemma.conclusion: Every trajectory from any state reaches that unique cycle in at most |S| transitions; therefore convergence after any one-step shock entering S does not identify selective punishment.
structural_lemma.proof: Each state has one successor. Following successors from any initial state must repeat a state in finite time; repeated states form a directed cycle. Uniqueness of the terminal cycle forces arrival at it.
structural_lemma.scope: For original 15x15=225 state frozen greedy joint policy only; no proof about transient cost, intentions, stationary equilibrium or agents outside S.

research_limits: Author-exported derived 1024-row CSV, not original converged Q tables or new training.
No independent recomputation of basins, counterfactual shocks or Bellman best-response.
Best-response gains have been rounded to two decimal places by source.
Pairs in authored dataset cannot be assumed independent population draws for frequentist inference.
Economic incentives and third-party welfare cannot be inferred from these numerical columns.
